world.bio: I'm Teresa Marques, born in Lisbon, and I run a six-room guesthouse called Casa das Janelas in a tiled nineteenth-century building in Alfama. I took it over from my aunt twelve years ago. Breakfast is homemade: bread from the corner bakery, my own orange marmalade, strong coffee. Guests come from everywhere; the regulars come back every spring.
skills_assets: Six-room guesthouse in Alfama, licensed as Alojamento Local
Twelve years of hosting, good reviews (9.2 on Booking)
Speaks Portuguese, English, French, basic German
A small team: one cleaner (Dona Lurdes) and a part-time receptionist (Tiago)
A tiled rooftop terrace with a view of the river

projects.name: Alojamento Local licence letter
projects.text: Last month the câmara sent a letter about new short-term rental rules. I have read it three times and still cannot tell whether my licence is affected: the letter mentions 'containment areas' and 'renewal', but my building is in a historic zone. I called the office twice and was put on hold. My accountant said she'd look, but she's busy with year-end.

projects.name: Terrace repair
projects.text: The terrace tiles need re-grouting before winter. Got a quote of 3,200 euros from a local mason. Not urgent, but the rain last week came through the ceiling of room 5.

notes.text: August is finally over. I slept ten hours yesterday and woke up feeling hungover from sleep. Full house every night for six weeks, 38 degrees on the terrace, a guest who complained about the church bells. I smiled and offered a second coffee.
Read the câmara letter again. 'Zonas de contenção.' 'Renovação do registo.' I cannot work out which sentence applies to me. Put it in the drawer with the other letters I fear.

My old podengo, Bolacha, has arthritis and hates the stairs. I carried him down this morning like a baby. The vet said joint supplements, 40 euros a month. He looked at me as if he'd forgive me for anything.

Tuesday guitar lesson with Senhor Alberto from next door. Portuguese guitar is not like Spanish; the strings are paired, the sound is a tear. My fingers hurt. He said 'fado is patience,' then took a sip of his ginjinha.
Room 3 guests, a young Dutch couple, left a note: 'This is the nicest place we've stayed.' Stuck it on the fridge next to the vaccination card.
Dona Lurdes' knees are getting worse. She cleans six rooms in four hours but I can see her limping. I don't know how to tell her to slow down without hurting her pride.

Cousin Manuel called to complain that the family building should be sold now while prices are high. I said it is not 'the family building', it's my home and my work. He sighed. We have had this conversation every year.
Rain all day. Sat in the empty breakfast room making marmalade. The kitchen smelled of oranges and sugar. This is why I do it.
Booking.com sent a new email about 'sustainability badges.' Another thing to fill in, another thing to pay for.
Autumn light on the tiles at four o'clock is the best thing in Lisbon. A guest took a photo of me at the window without asking. I let him.

messages.text:
Sofia: Teresa, I got the letter. I'll look at it next week.
Me: Thank you, I'm worried.
Sofia: Don't be. These letters always sound scarier than they are.

Tiago: Room 2 wants a late checkout.
Me: Give them until noon, no more.
Tiago: Noon it is.

Manuel: Have you thought about the offer?
Me: What offer?
Manuel: The Spanish group. They offered 1.8 million.
Me: No.

Alberto: Tuesday, same time. Bring your own tea.
Me: I will, and a pastel de nata.

Guest: We'd love room 5 again in April.
Me: It's yours. I'll fix the ceiling by then.

relations.about: Cleaner for nine years, loyal, bad knees
Wants to sell the building, keeps asking

constraints: Cannot leave the guesthouse for more than two days in high season
No short-term sublets to party groups
sensitive: Frightened that the new rules might end her licence and her income
Tired in a way a holiday does not cure
